findings.title: Recurring calendar deletions are started in an async forEach and never awaited
findings.body: In the recurring-cancellation branch, calendar deletions are performed inside `.forEach(async (credential) => { ... })`. `forEach` does not wait for async callbacks, so the request can continue and return before the external calendar events are deleted. It also means the asynchronous pushes into `apiDeletes` may happen after the later `Promise.all`/await has already run, and any rejection from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` becomes an unhandled promise rejection.

findings.title: Reschedule deletion loop is fire-and-forget
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` awaits `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` inside the callback, but the mutation never awaits the promises returned by the async callbacks. The function proceeds to send reschedule emails and webhooks before the calendar/video events are necessarily deleted, and any error thrown during those deletions is swallowed/unhandled.

findings.title: try/catch cannot catch errors from async forEach
findings.body: The deletion loop uses `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)`. Because `forEach` does not await async callbacks, the surrounding `try/catch` will not catch promise rejections from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting`, and the reschedule flow returns without waiting for the external deletions to complete.

findings.title: try/catch cannot catch errors from async forEach
findings.body: The deletion loop uses `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)`. Because `forEach` does not await async callbacks, the surrounding `try/catch` will not catch promise rejections from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting`, and the reschedule flow returns without waiting for the external deletions to complete.

findings.title: Awaiting an array does not await its promises
findings.body: `await apiDeletes;` awaits the array object itself, not the promises inside it. In the paid-cancellation path, integration deletion promises are therefore not waited on, so the handler can return before calendars/videos are cleaned up and rejected deletion promises may become unhandled. This should be `await Promise.all(apiDeletes);`.

findings.title: Video adapter loading is outside the fallback try/catch
findings.body: `createMeeting` awaits `getVideoAdapters([credential])` before the `try` block that falls back to Cal Video. With dynamic imports, `getVideoAdapters` can reject if an app module fails to load; that rejection bypasses the fallback logic and makes meeting creation fail hard instead of degrading to the default video provider.

findings.title: Eager dynamic imports create possibly unhandled rejected promises
findings.body: The appStore object immediately invokes `import(...)` for every app when the module is loaded. If any app module fails to load or throws during evaluation, its promise becomes rejected. Since not every app promise is necessarily awaited in every request, this can produce unhandled promise rejections. It also starts loading all apps even when only one is needed.

findings.title: Dynamic import failures cause getCalendar to throw instead of returning null
findings.body: `getCalendar` awaits `appStore[...]` without catching dynamic-import failures. A rejected app import will make `getCalendar` reject rather than returning `null`. Callers such as `getCachedResults` use `Promise.all`, so one broken calendar integration can fail all calendar operations instead of being treated as unavailable.

findings.title: lastAttendee condition is always false
findings.body: The condition checks `.length < 0`, which can never be true. If the intent is to detect that no other attendees remain, it should be `.length === 0`. As written, the branch that deletes integrations and marks the booking cancelled for the last attendee can never run.
